newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-NEWCOMBE IGNORES RANKINGS FOR FRANCE TIE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-NEWCOMBE IGNORES RANKINGS FOR FRANCE TIE.

text.p: French captain Yannick Noah's quest for a third Davis Cup title appeared to receive a boost on Thursday when his Australian counterpart ignored rankings in selecting his side for the first round tie starting on Friday.
Australia captain John Newcombe named doubles specialist Mark Woodforde and Patrick Rafter as his singles players ahead of the higher-ranked Todd Woodbridge.
Woodbridge is ranked 32 in singles, compared with Woodforde at 45 and Rafter at 64, and has been in good form in practice over the past week.
Rafter was drawn to play French number one Cedric Pioline in Friday's first singles rubber at Sydney's White City grass courts, followed by Woodforde against Arnaud Boetsch.
Woodbridge and Woodforde, who took their 42nd career doubles title at last month's Australian Open, will play Guy Forget and Guillaume Raoux in Saturday's doubles.
The Australians begin the tie without two of their best singles players after big-serving Mark Philippoussis and Jason Stoltenberg withdrew injured.

Newcombe told a news conference that Woodforde, who won three and lost nine of his previous 12 Davis Cup singles matches, had not been considered a likely singles choice when the team began practising a week ago.
"Mark's got the best record against the French guys, and he's also a left-hander and left-handers traditionally do well at White City," said Newcombe in explaining his selection.
"Pat over the last nine days has gradually been getting better and better each day. We felt this was the best combination to get the job done for us," he said.
Woodbridge, who last year won the Wimbledon, U.S. Open and Olympic doubles titles with Woodforde, admitted to being disappointed at missing out on the singles.

Noah named an unchanged team from that which won a thrilling final 3-2 over Sweden in Malmo last December. He thought Australia would start as favourites even though France had won the title under his tutelage last year and in 1991.
Pioline's world singles ranking of 26 and Boetsch's 31 are also superior to those of the Australians.
"They are the favourites because they have...the best doubles team in the world and they are playing at home on their surface," Noah said.

Newcombe disagreed, saying the tie would be a difficult one for Australia, who are back in the elite 16-team world group after being relegated to regional qaulifiers two years ago. "The French are the champions, we're just the battlers," he said.
The draw was as follows (French names first):

Friday's singles (first match starts at 0000 GMT) Cedric Pioline v Pat Rafter, Arnaud Boetsch v Mark Woodforde. Saturday's doubles (starts 0200 GMT) Guy Forget/Guillaume Raoux v Woodforde/Todd Woodbridge. Sunday's singles (start 0000 GMT) Woodforde v Pioline, Rafter v Boetsch.
